title: Guiding AI to Fix Its Own Flaws: An Empirical Study on LLM-Driven Secure Code Generation
abstract: arXiv:2506.23034v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models have become powerful tools for programming. However, they often overlook essential security practices, producing insecure code with vulnerabilities. Despite this risk, existing work offers limited guidance on steering LLMs toward secure code generation and lacks systematic analysis of how effectively LLMs repair vulnerable code. In this work, we investigate how LLMs can be guided to prevent and repair security vulnerabilities during code generation. Specifically, we examine whether self-generated vulnerability hints help models avoid insecure code, and evaluate how different feedback levels influence post-hoc vulnerability repair. Our study considers proprietary and open-weight models across multiple scales and uses established benchmarks covering diverse vulnerability types. translated_title: 引导AI修复自身缺陷：关于大语言模型驱动的安全代码生成的实证研究
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）已成为强大的编程工具。然而，它们往往忽视基本的安全实践，生成带有漏洞的不安全代码。尽管存在这一风险，现有工作在引导LLM生成安全代码方面提供的指导有限，且缺乏对LLM修复漏洞代码有效性的系统性分析。在本研究中，我们探讨了如何引导LLM在代码生成过程中预防和修复安全漏洞。具体而言，我们研究了自生成的漏洞提示是否能帮助模型避免生成不安全代码，并评估了不同反馈级别对事后漏洞修复效果的影响。我们的研究涵盖了专有模型和开源权重的模型，包括多种规模，并使用了覆盖多种漏洞类型的成熟基准测试。结果表明，自生成的漏洞提示能显著减少不安全代码，其有效性在很大程度上取决于提示的相关性。
tldr: 本实证研究表明，利用自生成的漏洞提示可以有效引导大语言模型减少不安全代码的生成，且不同反馈级别会影响其事后修复漏洞代码的效果。
en_tdlr: This empirical study shows that self-generated vulnerability hints can effectively guide LLMs to reduce insecure code generation, with effectiveness depending on hint relevance, and different feedback levels influence post-hoc vulnerability repair.
